about: The authors' twelve Readings, quoted from lean/BSmtLibSpec.lean ('List of readings'), each split into what the standard leaves open (gap) and what the Lean decides (choice). A matcher recovers a Reading when its own words identify both, on a declaration the authors attach the Reading to; it partly recovers it when it identifies the gap but not the choice, or only some of the parts; otherwise it misses it. Graded by Claude (Opus 5.5) with the authors' text visible, so the grades are a reviewed judgement, not a blind measurement.

L1.authors: consecutive non-parenthesis tokens must be separated (maximal-munch not allowed).
L1.gap: the standard does not say how adjacent tokens are separated
choice: a token other than a parenthesis must be followed by a parenthesis, whitespace or a comment, so 123abc is not a numeral followed by a symbol

L2.authors: an unterminated comment at the end of the input is not an error.
L2.gap: a comment ends with a line-breaking character, but the standard does not say that one must follow
choice: a comment running to the end of the input is accepted

L3.authors: a letter is `a` to `z` or `A` to `Z`.
L3.gap: 2.5 Appendix B writes the letter rule as A | ··· | A | a | ··· | z
choice: the letters are A to Z and a to z

L4.authors: a simple symbol excludes reserved words.
L4.gap: only 2.7 Appendix B excludes reserved words from simple symbols; earlier versions say so in §3.1 only
choice: simple symbols exclude reserved words in every version

L5.authors: a keyword is `:` followed by simple-symbol characters, allowing reserved words and leading digits but not an empty continuation.
L5.gap: from 2.5, Appendix B makes a keyword : followed by a simple symbol, which forbids a leading digit or a reserved word, yet the standard gives :56 as a keyword
choice: reserved words allowed after the colon
a lone colon is not a keyword

L6.authors: `define-funs-rec` is a command name (and a reserved word) from 2.5 on.
L6.gap: define-funs-rec is a command from 2.5 but is missing from Appendix B's list of reserved words
choice: define-funs-rec is a reserved word from 2.5 on

L7.authors: a 2.0 string literal may contain TAB, CR, or LF.
L7.gap: 2.0 defines a string literal as printable ASCII characters, and TAB, CR and LF are not printable
choice: a 2.0 string literal may contain TAB, CR or LF

L8.authors: the limitation of 2.0 to US-ASCII limits the input, not the lexicon.
choice: the limit applies to the input (the driver's responsibility), not to the lexical categories

G1.authors: before 2.6, a reserved word is not an s-expression.
G1.gap: in 2.0 and 2.5, §3.2's prose includes reserved words as s-expressions but the ⟨s_expr⟩ production does not
choice: the production is followed: before 2.6 a reserved word is not an s-expression

M1.authors: a version declaration changes the syntax mode between commands after the closing parenthesis of the `set-info` command; a declaration of a version that is not supported (such as 3.0) cannot stand in a file; `:smt-lib-version` declares the version in all SMT-LIB 2 versions including 2.0 and 2.5 which do not state this explicitly.
M1.gap: the standard does not say that or when a version declaration changes how the rest of the input is read
choice: the switch happens after the set-info command's closing parenthesis
an unsupported version cannot stand in a file

M2.authors: `exit` ends a script; the input after it is not parsed.
M2.gap: the standard only says exit makes the solver exit
choice: the input after (exit) is not parsed

M3.authors: `reset` does not return to the initial version.
M3.gap: the standard does not say what reset does to a declared version
choice: a version declared before reset still holds after it
